claim: The first diffusion tensor images of brain tissue showed diffusion anisotropy in white matter.
source: The first diffusion tensor images of brain tissue showed diffusion anisotropy in white matter (Basser et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by citation to Basser et al., 1994

claim: Diffusion anisotropy in white matter is due to myelin membranes and other cellular components impeding water mobility more in the direction perpendicular to the oriented fibers than parallel to them.
source: It was postulated that this anisotropy is due to myelin membranes and other cellular components impeding water mobility more in the direction perpendicular to the oriented fibers than parallel to them.
evidence: Presented as a postulation from historical context

claim: Beaulieu and Allen (1994) concluded that the origin of diffusion anisotropy in white matter is due to membranes.
source: By process of elimination, Beaulieu and Allen (1994) concluded that the origin of diffusion anisotropy in white matter is due to membranes (Beaulieu, 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to Beaulieu and Allen (1994) and Beaulieu (2002)

claim: Diffusion becomes isotropic and diffusivity approaches the value of free water after complete delipidation.
source: New methods to clear lipid membranes while leaving other tissue components intact (Chung et al., 2013; Tainaka et al., 2018) have confirmed directly that diffusion becomes isotropic and diffusivity approaches the value of free water after complete delipidation (Leuze et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chung et al., 2013; Tainaka et al., 2018; and Leuze et al., 2017

claim: Spin magnetization retains the history of motions encoded during the experimental pulse sequence.
source: A characteristic of MR is that spin magnetization retains the history of motions encoded during the experimental pulse sequence (Callaghan et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Callaghan et al., 2007

claim: Diffusion MR measures the spin echo signal attenuation of nuclear spins which displace randomly in the presence of a magnetic field gradient.
source: Diffusion MR measures the spin echo (Hahn, 1950) signal attenuation of nuclear spins which displace randomly in the presence of a magnetic field gradient (Carr and Purcell, 1954; Callaghan et al., 1991; Callaghan, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hahn, 1950; Carr and Purcell, 1954; Callaghan et al., 1991; Callaghan, 2011

claim: The displacements contain averaged information about the hindrances and restrictions which the molecules experienced during their random trajectories through the microstructure.
source: The displacements contain averaged information about the hindrances and restrictions which the molecules experienced during their random trajectories through the microstructure.
evidence: Based on established understanding of diffusion MR

claim: The diffusion MR signal of water in heterogeneous materials such as biological tissue contains a multitude of components arising from water in different microenvironments.
source: The diffusion MR signal of water in heterogeneous materials such as biological tissue would be expected to contain a multitude of components arising from water in different microenvironments, which restrict water diffusion to varying degrees (Benjamini and Basser, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Benjamini and Basser, 2017

claim: Nonparametric data inversion techniques can model signal attenuation as arising from distributions of diffusion coefficients.
source: Nonparametric data inversion techniques can model signal attenuation as arising from distributions of diffusion coefficients (Pfeuffer et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pfeuffer et al., 1999

claim: The diffusion coefficient distribution can be used to investigate the microstructural properties of neural tissue.
source: Pfeuffer et al. (1999), along with Ronen et al. (2006) and Benjamini and Basser (2019), suggest that the diffusion coefficient distribution can be used to investigate the microstructural properties of neural tissue.
evidence: Supported by citations to Pfeuffer et al., 1999; Ronen et al., 2006; Benjamini and Basser, 2019

claim: Exchange can be measured from the change in apparent diffusion coefficients with encoding time.
source: Exchange can be measured from the change in apparent diffusion coefficients with encoding time (Andrasko, 1976; Kärger et al., 1988; Waldeck et al., 1995; Pfeuffer et al., 1998; Thelwall et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to Andrasko, 1976; Kärger et al., 1988; Waldeck et al., 1995; Pfeuffer et al., 1998; Thelwall et al., 2002

claim: There is some redundancy in the DEXSY data.
source: Recent research shows that there is some redundancy in the data (Bai et al., 2016a; Benjamini and Basser, 2016; Benjamini and Basser, 2018; Benjamini et al., 2017) and alternative DEXSY-based approaches may measure exchange with fewer data points (Aslund et al., 2009; Benjamini et al., 2017; Cai et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bai et al., 2016a; Benjamini and Basser, 2016; Benjamini and Basser, 2018; Benjamini et al., 2017

claim: DEXSY-based methods measure the permeability of cell membranes to water.
source: Aslund et al. (2009) and Lasič et al. (2011) showed DEXSY-based methods measure the permeability of cell membranes to water.
evidence: Supported by citations to Aslund et al., 2009 and Lasič et al., 2011

claim: Larger gradient strengths and gradient durations probe smaller structures.
source: Larger gradient strengths and gradient durations probe smaller structures (Callaghan et al., 1991).
evidence: Supported by citation to Callaghan et al., 1991

claim: Hardware constraints cap the maximum strength of gradient coils of MRI systems at a few Tesla/m.
source: Hardware constraints cap the maximum strength of gradient coils of MRI systems at a few Tesla/m.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of MRI hardware limitations

claim: Diffusion MR microstructural resolution is predicted to be limited to structures larger than a few microns with long gradient pulse durations and encoding times.
source: With long gradient pulse durations and encoding times, diffusion MR microstructural resolution is predicted to be limited to structures larger than a few microns (Nilsson et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nilsson et al., 2017

claim: When water within structures exchanges on a timescale faster than the diffusion encoding time, the structure sizes appear inflated.
source: However, when water within these structures exchanges on a timescale faster than the diffusion encoding time, the structure sizes appear inflated.
evidence: Based on inference from diffusion MR theory

claim: In the extreme case of fast exchange, the structures are no longer visible as attenuation measures only the mean diffusivity.
source: In the extreme case of fast exchange, the structures are no longer visible as attenuation measures only the mean diffusivity (Kärger et al., 1988; Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kärger et al., 1988; Yang et al., 2018

claim: Gradient pulses last at least a millisecond, which sets a lower limit for the encoding time.
source: Gradient pulses last at least a millisecond, which sets a lower limit for the encoding time (Price, 1998).

claim: An experiment performed in a strong static gradient field can break the microstructural resolution limit.

evidence: Supported by citations to Hahn, 1950; Carr and Purcell, 1954; Kimmich et al., 1991

claim: Low-cost, portable, bench-top, single-sided NMR devices with greater than 10 T/m static gradients can probe sub-micron structures.

evidence: Supported by citations to Eidmann et al., 1996; Carlton et al., 2000; Potter et al., 1996

claim: Displacement encoding within a static gradient field occurs by using radiofrequency (RF) pulses to switch the 'effective gradient', allowing for diffusion encoding times as short as 100 μs.
source: Displacement encoding within a static gradient field occurs by using radiofrequency (RF) pulses (Hahn, 1950; Carr and Purcell, 1954) to switch the 'effective gradient' (Callaghan, 2011), allowing for diffusion encoding times as short as 100 μs (Stepišnik et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hahn, 1950; Carr and Purcell, 1954; Callaghan, 2011; Stepišnik et al., 2018

claim: In the solenoid coil, the spinal cord is oriented with its length perpendicular to the gradient such that the system measures diffusion of water perpendicular to the spinal cord.
source: In the solenoid coil, the spinal cord is oriented with its length perpendicular to the gradient such that the system measures diffusion of water perpendicular to the spinal cord.

claim: After removing restrictions, hindrances to water diffusion can be thought of as arising from volume obstruction by biomacromolecules such as proteins within the tissue.

source: Structures smaller than 1400 nm include cells and portions of cells with small radii such as axons, dendrites, glial processes, myelin, and a number of membranous organelles such as nuclei, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticula, and vesicles (Kandel et al., 2013), in addition to extracellular sheets and tunnels (Kinney et al., 2013).
